paper_metadata.title: Effect of Cr Additions on Toughness, Strength, and Oxidation Resistance of an Nb-4Si-20Ti-6Hf Alloy at Room and/or High Temperatures

evidence.quote: Nb is one of the most promising refractory metals for the next generation of ultrahigh-temperature structural materials

both the Cr concentration in the Nb SS phase and volume fraction of the brittle silicides increases with an increase of the nominal Cr content. These metallurgical changes may affect the bulk toughness at low temperatures, strength at elevated temperatures, and environmental stability (oxidation resistance) of the Nb-Si-based alloys.

Button ingots of the Nb-4Si-20Ti-6Hf-(6,10,14)Cr alloys (referred to 6Cr alloy, 10Cr alloy, and 14Cr alloy, respectively, hereafter) each with a weight of 100 g were prepared by arc melting five or six times in an argon atmosphere under a pressure of ~0.5 Pa.
The ingots were annealed finally at 1648 K (1375 °C) in vacuum for 100 hours and then furnace cooled to ensure quasi-equilibrium microstructures.

mechanisms.name: intergranular deflection and branching of the crack

evidence.quote: Thus, one can determine that the intergranular deﬂection and branching of the crack are the main toughening mechanisms of the Nb SS-dominant Nb SS/silicides microstructures.
The previous analysis suggests strongly that Cr additions strengthen the Nb SS phase, which is favorable to the bulk strength of the Nb-Si-based alloys at room temperature.
It was reported that internal oxidation is the main oxidation mechanism of the Nb SS phase, which is relative to the oxygen dissolved in the Nb SS phase.
